1.explanation: Both files define the Markdown language grammar for Prism. The non-minified file (prism-markdown.js) contains the regex rules and token definitions for headings, links, code spans, etc., but currently lacks an image rule to match `![alt](url)`. The minified file is the production build of the same grammar and must be updated in lockstep with its source. By adding or extending the image pattern in prism-markdown.js (and then re-minifying), Prism will correctly parse and highlight image tokens.
1.bug_scenario: When writing Markdown with an image token (e.g. `![emoji](https://content.markdowner.net/emoji/g/64/1f44d.png)`), Prism’s Markdown grammar doesn’t recognize the leading exclamation mark (`!`) and the entire image syntax is treated as plain text or as a link rather than an “image” token. As a result, the code block shows the raw Markdown but doesn’t highlight it correctly or distinguish it from link syntax.

2.explanation: Both files define the Markdown language grammar for Prism. The un-minified version (prism-markdown.js) is where the image pattern must be added (a regex to match `![alt](url)`), and the minified file must be updated in parallel to reflect that change for browser builds.
2.bug_scenario:
When rendering Markdown source that contains an image token—e.g.:

    ![emoji](https://content.markdowner.net/emoji/g/64/1f44d.png)

Prism’s current Markdown grammar does not recognize the image syntax (alt text in brackets and URL in parentheses) as a distinct token, so neither the alt text nor the URL is highlighted or classified properly.
